smell_validity.evidence: The same ~10 listing controls (limit, offset, type, worker, state, sort_by, descending, received window, search) thread as loose positional args through iter_tasks, search_tasks, _filter_task_ids, _page_results and both surface intakes. The desc states they 'flow as a row of loose individual arguments through every signature.' Values clearly belong together; cost (one control = editing every signature, two threading conventions aligned by hand) is clear. Boundary from healthy design is described, not self-evident.

maintenance_impact.evidence: Adding a control means editing the argument row in every signature and keeping two threading conventions (positional row vs explicit None fills) aligned by hand, plus keeping derived sort direction consistent across surfaces. This is a lasting trap that obscures what belongs together; the abstraction restores a single ownership boundary. Not architecture-level, but clearly beyond local convenience.

development_plausibility.evidence: Modeled as review-sized convergence steps (extract duplicated control handling, explicit sort direction, split engine entry, add page translation seam) — believable pay-down of duplication. Flower REST + DataTables domain fits; positional 10-arg threading is a plausible compromise emerging from the refactor, not its goal. Fits the repo's style and terminology; minimal task-shaped scaffolding.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: Explicit prompt names the problem (controls unowned), full scope (REST endpoint, tasks page, helper module, indexed core), the finished state (one coherent value through internal layers), and firm constraints (REST/tasks-page contracts, engine keyword protocol as boundary, no test changes). Rules out partial cleanups ('cleanup only counts if threading gone from internal layers') without prescribing one implementation.

semantic_diversity.evidence: At least three purposes need different decisions: the filter phase (posting-index intersections plus time window), the order/page phase (ordering-key choice, offset clamp, top-N heap, result page), and normalization (sentinel/prefix/offset conventions) applied differently per surface. Surface translations differ — REST derives direction from -prefix; the page supplies it explicitly.

localization_burden.evidence: Calls flow across the helper module and the indexed engine; solver must follow iter_tasks to search_tasks to engine.search to _filter/_page and decide the engine's public keyword signature is a boundary (excluded) while internal phases are repaired. The prompt already names all four components and the engine boundary, limiting discovery to the internal call chain.

repair_coordination.evidence: Two shared rules must be preserved across locations: normalization (All sentinel, -prefix, offset clamp) applied exactly once, and sort-direction derivation kept consistent between the REST surface (derived) and the page surface (explicit). Absorbing normalize_task_query into each surface's value construction must not reintroduce double application or drop a convention.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: One uniform value type threads through the internal helper/engine-phase signatures (iter_tasks, search_tasks, _filter_task_ids, _page_results), but the engine public search() keeps individual keyword args (boundary, must unpack) and the two surface intakes need different value-construction code (REST normalizes, page fills None). Roughly half of the row-restating locations yield to one uniform rule.

behavioral_risk.evidence: A wrong repair that drops the -prefix to descending derivation on the REST path, or the All to None mapping, passes ordinary ascending/no-filter calls but silently fails in special state (descending sort requested or All filter sent) with a comparable-but-wrong result or ordering. It requires specific input to surface, not caught by ordinary calls.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
